Functions of Bounded Variation

This scene measures the total distance a function wiggles. If that sum stays under a finite ceiling, the function has bounded variation.

Start and finish alone are not enough. Every up and down in between must be added. Monotone functions pass since they wiggle one way only. Endless trembling makes the sum explode.

For example, a 🚗 car driving up and down has bounded variation while its total mileage stays definite. Trembling in place forever would pile the distance up without end.

Show proof

  1. Let fff be increasing on [a,b][a, b][a,b] and take any partition P={x0<x1<⋯<xm}P = \{x_0 < x_1 < \dots < x_m\}P={x0​<x1​<⋯<xm​} ([x0,xm]=[a,b][x_0, x_m] = [a, b][x0​,xm​]=[a,b]). Monotonicity gives f(xi)−f(xi−1)≥0f(x_i) - f(x_{i-1}) \ge 0f(xi​)−f(xi−1​)≥0 on each subinterval, so the absolute values unwrap: ∑i=1m∣f(xi)−f(xi−1)∣=∑i=1m(f(xi)−f(xi−1))\sum_{i=1}^{m}|f(x_i) - f(x_{i-1})| = \sum_{i=1}^{m}(f(x_i) - f(x_{i-1}))∑i=1m​∣f(xi​)−f(xi−1​)∣=∑i=1m​(f(xi​)−f(xi−1​)), which telescopes to f(b)−f(a)f(b) - f(a)f(b)−f(a).

  2. The decreasing case is the same: f(xi)−f(xi−1)≤0f(x_i) - f(x_{i-1}) \le 0f(xi​)−f(xi−1​)≤0, so ∣f(xi)−f(xi−1)∣=f(xi−1)−f(xi)|f(x_i) - f(x_{i-1})| = f(x_{i-1}) - f(x_i)∣f(xi​)−f(xi−1​)∣=f(xi−1​)−f(xi​) and the sum is f(a)−f(b)=∣f(b)−f(a)∣f(a) - f(b) = |f(b) - f(a)|f(a)−f(b)=∣f(b)−f(a)∣. Every partition of a monotone fff gives the same variation ∣f(b)−f(a)∣|f(b) - f(a)|∣f(b)−f(a)∣.

  3. Hence the supremum over partitions is ∣f(b)−f(a)∣<∞|f(b) - f(a)| < \infty∣f(b)−f(a)∣<∞, i.e. Vab(f)=∣f(b)−f(a)∣V_a^b(f) = |f(b) - f(a)|Vab​(f)=∣f(b)−f(a)∣: monotone functions are of bounded variation. The Cantor function (see the limits chapter) is increasing on [0,1][0, 1][0,1] with c(0)=0c(0) = 0c(0)=0, c(1)=1c(1) = 1c(1)=1, so V01(c)=1V_0^1(c) = 1V01​(c)=1.

Jordan decomposition: fff is of bounded variation on [a,b][a, b][a,b] if and only if f=g−hf = g - hf=g−h with g,hg, hg,h increasing on [a,b][a, b][a,b].
